name_reason: Compliant with the global naming convention: data_fd2_ prefix + battle domain (battle core pathfind table) + descriptor pathfind_map_height that reflects both purpose (battle-map height in tiles) and that it is a scalar dimension/count. No Ghidra address residue (the trailing 'height' is a semantic word, not a hex of its own address 0x60069 or any data address). It is the down-direction bound counterpart of data_fd2_battle_pathfind_map_width (0x60068), and the name pairs cleanly with it.
purpose: Runtime battle-map height in tiles; used as the unsigned down-direction bound in the movement-range flood-fill and the destination pathfinder.
logic_summary: Single unsigned byte at 0x60069 (.object3 BSS, adjacent to map_width at 0x60068). Both pathfind orchestrators (fd2_init_movement_range_floodfill, fd2_pathfind_to_destination) write it at entry from the tile-map header byte [tile_map_ptr + 2]. The two recursive expanders read it 8-bit and use it unsigned as the down-direction bound: (uint8)(y + 1) < map_height (disasm at 0x4E2E1: INC DH; CMP DH,[0x60069]; JNC skip). Write-before-read, so the load-time zero is never observed.
element_semantics: Scalar: number of tile rows in the active battle map (map height in tiles). Not an array (0x60068 is the separate map_width field; 0x6006A begins the caller_context pointer).
notes: Verified via Ghidra MCP: datatype=byte len=1, memory=0 (BSS .object3 image), 4 xrefs (WRITE 0x4E078 + 0x4E1FE from the two orchestrators; READ 0x4E12C + 0x4E2E1 from the two recursive expanders). is_const=false because the game writes it at runtime (2 WRITE xrefs); src correctly emits a plain non-const uint8. The pre-existing Ghidra data plate lived in the legacy PRE_COMMENT field (PLATE_COMMENT was null) and carried a stale 'emit_action = emit_c_const' line that contradicts the verified non-const reality; created a proper PLATE_COMMENT (src-consistent, marks it NOT const) via run_script_inline + cu.setComment(PLATE_COMMENT,..), cleared the stale PRE_COMMENT, and ran save_program() (success). Src comment block (lines 781-790 of pathfnd.c) already accurate and precise -> keep, src not modified.
